correctness.rationale: Definitions determine exactly a 30-vertex graph. Every perfect matching is a distinct 15-row duad-to-syntheme incidence bijection; exhaustive recursion lists all 288. Relative-permutation cycles identify precisely eight-cycle exchanges. Independent explicit cycle-flip enumeration finds the same 1440 adjacency pairs with SHA-256 ba8739d1315a1daa2d3810948317a38cdf47b81a8cd37f5377e6825b7136e6a3. All-vertex BFS gives the two profiles, radius five and diameter six; all 41328 unordered pairs verify the equivalence of distance six with a Hamiltonian symmetric difference. Both standalone programs were executed and their complete outputs matched the embedded stdout files. Finite exhaustive proof and numerical scope are explicit in RESULT.md.

evidence: Dyer–Jerrum–Müller (arxiv:1501.07725) define a switch as a 2-by-2 alternating swap, i.e. a four-cycle; their hereditary ergodicity and mixing results concern that move model.

Ito et al. (arxiv:1907.01700), Introduction and Sections 3–4: shortest paths under unrestricted alternating-cycle flips, polynomial-time outerplanar cases and NP-hardness for general planar and bipartite graphs.
The Tutte–Coxeter graph has girth eight, so no four-cycle switches exist; unrestricted alternating-cycle adjacency also differs from fixed eight-cycle adjacency.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem of general complexity or ergodicity for other move rules does not imply the exact 288-vertex distance partition here. The outerplanar distance formula is not applicable to the non-outerplanar cubic girth-eight cage, and it allows arbitrary cycle lengths. Both primary papers were checked for a named Tutte–Coxeter instance without a matching instance found.

value.rationale: The unique cubic girth-eight cage and generalized-quadrangle incidence graph is a canonical object; its absence of smaller cycles makes the first available flip length eight mathematically forced. The finding identifies the sharp first connected flip dynamics, an exact two-stratum full metric profile, and a Hamiltonian-union characterization of every diametral pair. These data are not scalar matching counts, cosmetic renaming, or a routine parameter increment; they exhibit a concrete relationship between complementary two-factor structure and restricted reconfiguration distance. No infinite-graph extrapolation is made.
